Subject: Trial extension & unused quota question

Hi Neha,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — the team loved the latency and cost breakdown you shared. We're running low on tokens for the POC and have one week left on the current time-box. Two quick asks: 1) would Redwood consider a short extension (2 weeks) so we can finish the integration tests? 2) if we don't use all of the allocated tokens during the extended window, can they be converted to account credits that we can draw down when/if we convert to a paid plan?

Thanks,

Hi Emma — really glad the demo landed. Quick answers up front and two proposed paths so you can pick what fits BrightHealth: 

Option A — Time extension + small conversion credit
- 3 week extension to the POC (adds runway to finish integration testing)
- Convert up to 25% of unused committed tokens during the extension into a $3,000 account credit if you convert to a 6-month committed plan within 60 days

Option B — Rate-card adjustment (no extension)
- No time extension; instead we offer a temporary 15% pilot overage discount for the existing rate-card if you need a short buffer

Initial ask from my side: which of the two you prefer and whether procurement needs a formal addendum. If you want Option A, I can send a short pilot addendum (2 pages) that documents the extension and the credit trigger. I've attached a draft for your review.

I cc'd Marissa from pricing to keep the proposal aligned with quotas and billing. If you're happy with Option A we can route the addendum through DocuSign; if procurement wants a credits-first approach, we can surface the rate-card change in writing instead.

If helpful, we can also do a 20-minute touchpoint with your procurement team early next week.

Best,
Neha Kapoor

Neha / Marissa — quick internal note on margin and approval path.

- 3-week extension + $3k convertible credit (Option A) is fine commercially, but we need a one-off credit approval since it impacts billable run-rate if they convert to committed later. I can sign up to $3k; anything above that needs CRO sign-off.
- For legal: keep the addendum language simple — extension period, credit conversion trigger (explicit 60-day conversion window), and a one-line cap on total credit. No product SLA changes.
- Alternative: if procurement pushes back on credit language, offer 2-week no-cost extension + $2k account credit (smaller, easier approval).

If you want me to take this to finance for a faster sign-off, say the word and I'll attach the credits-approval-form.

Jonas
